input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 binds Customer, not Vendor: before engaging any other provider we must surrender the terms of a competing offer and give Vendor the chance to match. That is a right of first refusal amounting to de facto exclusivity (plus an MFC-style disclosure duty), which the playbook prohibits, and it compounds the Section 2.1 take-or-pay minimum by making it impractical to source elsewhere. It also directly contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment. Preferred position is deletion; a narrow category-limited 12-month first-look right with automatic termination on service-level or delivery failure is the fallback. The non-exclusive licence grants and Vendor-side exclusivity provisions elsewhere are unobjectionable.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the requirement to disclose and match third-party offers before engaging another provider: it operates as de facto exclusivity and a right of first refusal on us, which our playbook does not accept, and it contradicts Section 12.3 (no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment). If Cobalt needs something here, we could consider a narrow first-look right limited to a defined service category for 12 months that ends automatically if service levels or delivery dates are missed.
proposal.summary: Delete Section 7.2 disclose-and-match obligation that creates de facto exclusivity on Customer.
